newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol weighs major fuel expansion - report.
newsitem.headline: Sasol weighs major fuel expansion - report.

text.p: Synthetic fuel producer Sasol Ltd may spend over six billion rand to increase production of oil and chemical feedstocks by 45 percent over the next three years, according to chief executive Pieter Cox.

In an interview with the Financial Mail, published on Thursday, Cox said about 20 percent of the planned output hike would be available by 1999, when the company commissions its eight new-generation Advanced Synthol reactors at Secunda, at an estimated cost of one billion rand.
Sasol is also investigating a 25 percent expansion of the synfuel refinery at Secunda at a further cost of more five billion rand.
"While a 20 percent output hike might seem impressive, it will only be sufficient to meet one year's increase in domestic demand," said Cox.

South African demand for petroleum products is growing at about five to six percent a year. Sasol supplies some 32 percent of local demand for liquid fuels from its coal-based synthetic fuel plant at Secunda.
A further 10 percent of local supply comes from the Natref crude oil refinery at Sasolburg which Sasol jointly owns with Total SA.
Increased production would help meet not only a looming shortage of white oil products but also South Africa's growing demand for ethylene.
Cox added that the planned expansion depended on a successful renegotiation of Sasol's fuel supply agreement with the domestic oil industry which takes a specified volume of Sasol synfuel production.
